key_insight: Ultra-rare damaging variants in schizophrenia-associated genes were linked to less favorable clinical and functional trajectories across psychotic disorders, despite similar diagnostic distributions.
clinical_relevance: These variants may identify biological differences relevant to long-term care needs, but the findings do not establish a clinical genetic screening tool.
method: Screened 9,821 sequenced SUPER-Finland participants with psychotic disorders for ultra-rare damaging variants in 40 schizophrenia-associated genes.
Compared 163 carriers with non-carriers using five decades of nationwide health registers and enrollment assessments.
Examined outcomes alongside schizophrenia polygenic risk and damaging variants in other neurodevelopmental-disorder genes.
evidence_signal: Carriers had earlier psychiatric admissions (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.48–3.57) and non-psychiatric admissions (HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.10–1.79), alongside poorer cognitive performance and lower attainment of adult social milestones.
watch_item: This observational Finnish cohort supports associations, not causation or validated individual-level prediction; generalizability requires further study.
paper_title: Ultra-rare coding variants in schizophrenia risk genes are associated with longitudinal phenotypic differences across psychotic disorders
